column11: Bava Batra 123b: ‘Rabbi Ḥelbo raised an objection to Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani: Concering a battle between the Jewish people and the nation of Amalek, who descend from Esau, the verse states: “And David smote them from the twilight even to the evening of the next day” (I Samuel 30:17). column11: Yoma 28b: ‘Apropos the previous statement, the Gemara cites that Rav said: Abraham our Patriarch fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given, as it is stated: “Because [ekev] Abraham hearkened to My voice and kept My charge, My mitzvot, My statutes and My Torahs” (Genesis 26:5). column15: “And God said: Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, etc.” Behold, from these verses the distinction between the sustenance of man and that of beast is evident: for concerning human food it is written “herb yielding seed,” while concerning animal food it is written “green herb.” The explanation is as stated in the Holy Zohar (Bereishit 24b), that the worlds are arranged like the layers of an onion: meaning that each world is an outer garment for the realm above it, this physical world being a garment for the supernal world, ascending higher and higher to the Infinite.

Hence the Tanach considered it as if they were gentiles and remained forbidden. Moreover, their conduct ultimately revealed their initial intent. For they would worship their false deities and build platforms for them. Therefore the Scriptures considered it as if [Solomon] built them, as [I Kings 11:7] states: "And then, Solomon built a platform."’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this commentary and philosophical-halakhic exposition (Mishneh Torah, Forbidden Intercourse 13:16) to illuminate his exposition here (“And Maimonides (Hilchot Issurei Biah 13:16) wrote that Samson converted them, though the literal text implies otherwise, for on that his parents would not have objected, leaders of Israel having married female...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And when David fled before Absalom, thinking his eternal victory was lost; and that a king like him, the root and head of Malkhut, would be slain by his son, no longer living and enduring; and there is no greater desecration of the Name (Chillul Hashem) than this; for the Name of Hashem is His attribute of Kingship dwelling within the lower realms; what is perceived by creations being His Name, by which He is called according to their grasp; the Name having no independent existence apart from the divine Essence, this being the sanctification of the Name.
column15: And as my revered grandfather remarked: Why is it that in the psalm (Psalms 148) “Praise Hashem from the heavens,” the waters under the heaven are not mentioned — it explicitly mentions the upper waters, so why not the lower waters as well? And even though it says there “deeps” (tehomot), “deeps” does not refer to the water itself, but to the deep oceanic vessel that holds the water. Why then does it not list the lower waters themselves?

column11: Megillah 14b: ‘The Gemara asks: The plural term damim, literally, bloods, indicates two. Why did David not use the singular term dam? Rather, this teaches that Abigail revealed her thigh, and he lusted after her, and he went three parasangs by the fire of his desire for her, and said to her: Listen to me, i.e., listen to me and allow me to be intimate with you. Abigail then said to him: “Let this not be a stumbling block for you” (I Samuel 25:31). By inference, from the word “this,” it can be understood that there is someone else who will in fact be a stumbling block for him, and what is this referring to? The incident involving Bathsheba. And in the end this is what was, as indeed he stumbled with…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Megillah 14b) to illuminate his exposition here (“for on that his parents would not have objected, leaders of Israel having married female converts like Joshua marrying Rahab (Megillah 14b); and the Sages termed this rebellion, stating (Sotah 9b): she desired an...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: In Midrash Rabbah (Mishpatim, Parashah 30): The Holy One, blessed be He, sought to give them four things: Torah, afflictions, sacrificial service, and prayer; yet they did not desire them, as it is said: "And they said unto God: Depart from us"—these are afflictions; " "And the knowledge of Your ways we do not desire"—this is Torah; " "What is the Almighty that we should serve Him?"—these are the sacrifices; " "And what profit should we have if we pray to Him?"—this is prayer.
column15: Meaning, the essence of service exists solely because Hashem erected separating screens, and man, through Torah and spiritual labor, breaches the dividing screen and reaches the light of Hashem — that is the primary labor of humanity. And in truth, if a person breaks through all manner of screens and reaches the first explicit utterance termed “Let there be light,” then Hashem grants him a portion even in the transcendent utterance of “Bereishit,” concerning which it is taught in the Talmud (Megillah 21b): “Bereishit is also an utterance.”

column11: Sotah 9b: ‘The verse states: “And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart” (Judges 16:18). The Gemara asks: From where did she know that this time he had told her the truth about the source of his strength, as he had lied about it previously? Rabbi Ḥanin says that Rav says: Words of truth are recognizable, and she felt that this time he was telling the truth. Abaye says differently: She knew about Samson being a righteous individual, that he would not express the name of Heaven in vain. Once he said: “And he told her all his heart, and said to her: There has not come a razor upon my head; for I have been a nazirite unto God from my mother’s womb” (Judges 16:17), she said: Now he is…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Sotah 9b) to illuminate his exposition here (“and the Sages termed this rebellion, stating (Sotah 9b): she desired an impure thing. And although Mishneh LaMelech resolves this because they converted for a husband rather than Heaven and were improperly accepted,...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And thus what appeared as a departure from holiness was on the contrary the essence of holiness; turning after rectification to the hurt of the Corrupt Man, demonstrating that herein lies the core of holiness; this being an extraordinary power of holiness, remaining full of sanctity even amidst apparent departure, needing no defensive aid.
column14: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 10:11
column15: For in truth, it is not within man's mortal power to generate taste and delight in performing Hashem's mitzvah, as Scripture states (Psalms 36:8): “How precious is Your lovingkindness, O God!” 'Chesed' alludes to longing and desire for words of Torah and Hashem's commandments, and Scripture testifies that it is an exceedingly precious thing, and even an absolute righteous man cannot fabricate desire for Torah and mitzvot on his own, for otherwise it would not be termed 'precious.'

column11: Judges 14:3: ‘His father and mother said to him, “Is there no one among the daughters of your own kindred and among all our people, that you must go and take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” But Samson answered his father, “Get me that one, for she is the one that pleases me.”’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Judges 14:3) to illuminate his exposition here (“since Scripture and the Sages accounted them as gentiles, they are fittingly called "daughters of the uncircumcised" despite conversion, not being valid converts. And our Sages stated that his life was suspended upon...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Yet acknowledging that they lack the convert-soul to be titled Israel, being destined to serve as plowmen and vinedressers (Yeshayah 61:5); meriting eternal life to serve Israel in the World to Come because they recognized Israel's chosenness in this world, this being their root of good]; wherefore the Mishnah rules: "one who vows abstinence from the uncircumcised is forbidden unto circumcised gentiles" (Nedarim 31b)!
column15: From where do we derive this? From Joseph, in whom the power of constriction was preeminent, he being the first to give counsel to exercise restraint during the years of abundance so that reserves would remain for the years of famine. And as Scripture states (Genesis 41:35–36): “And let them gather all the food of those good years... and that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine,” concerning which Pharaoh said to him: “There is none so discreet and wise as you,” for this power of holy restraint is found not among the nations, but within Israel alone.

column11: Judges 15:19: ‘So God split open the hollow that is at Lehi, and the water gushed out of it; he drank, regained his strength, and revived. That is why it is called to this day “En-hakkore of Lehi.”’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Judges 15:19) to illuminate his exposition here (“And our Sages stated that his life was suspended upon an unclean thing, the jawbone of a donkey [Judges 15:19], because he desired that which is termed "flesh of donkeys"; and though a miracle was wrought giving him...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Riding the donkey symbolizes riding upon and governing one’s physical materiality. In truth, however, Balaam did not govern his material nature; he was drawn after it. The fourth prophecy, concerning the end of days, relates to the revelation of the residual imprint. Then Balaam said, “Behold, I am going to my people”: even after saying “may my soul die the death of the upright,” he sensed that at the end of days he still goes to his own people, for he lacks Israel’s inner imprint.
column14: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Deuteronomy, Re'eh 3
column15: “The blessing, if you follow .…” (Devarim, 11:27)If man receives good, then he clearly knows that he has fulfilled God’s will. If the opposite befalls him, God forbid, then he knows that surely he has transgressed the mitzvot of God, even if it does not seem so on the surface.

column11: Sotah 10a: ‘With regard to Samson’s capture, the verse states: “And the Philistines laid hold on him, and put out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison-house” (Judges 16:21). Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Grinding is nothing other than a language of a transgression of sexual intercourse, and so the verse says: “Then let my wife grind unto another man” (Job 31:10). This teaches that each and every Philistine man brought his wife to the prison in order that she should be impregnated by Samson. Rav Pappa said: This is an example of the folk saying that people say: Before a wine drinker, bring wine; before one who digs in the ground, bring…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Sotah 10a) to illuminate his exposition here (“all desire of the Philistines being to attach to Israel (Sotah 10a relating that every Philistine brought his wife to prison to conceive from him), as Abimelech and Pharaoh took Sarah. The matter is: Egypt is "the...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And even though he rectified the heart, he did not yet rectify the eyes, which are “the essential beginning”; and therefore they were “evil in the eyes of Hashem.” And in the matter of Tamar, which was through seeing — “and Yehudah saw her [and took her for a harlot]” (Bereishis 38:15) — he began to rectify the eyes; and it is known that they [Er and Onan] were reincarnated and rectified in Peretz and Zerach; and therefore it says of her, “and she sat at the opening of the eyes [pesach einayim]” (Bereishis 38:14) — this is the entry to the rectification of the eyes.

column15: You have drunk the wine—return the flagon to its place! And so we find conversely: fraud greater than a sixth, Heaven forbid, where the purchase is completely voided, like what we find in Esau, who arrogated unto himself excessive overconfidence, saying concerning himself (Obadiah 1:3): “you that dwell in the clefts of the rock... that say in his heart: Who shall bring me down to the ground?!”

column11: Genesis 10:14: ‘the Pathrusim, the Casluhim (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorim.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Genesis 10:14) to illuminate his exposition here (“The matter is: Egypt is "the nakedness of the land," the Yesod of the husk, and Egypt had seven sons, the sixth being Casluhim whence came the Philistines [Genesis 10:14], and every seven corresponds to the seven...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And "the nakedness of the land" denotes immersion in worldliness devoid of active labor, being mere passive dreamers lying down. And the absolute depths of this condition is termed "an outcast", who is not completely lost, for he is not consumed by alien conquests nor swallowed among the gentiles; yet he is nonetheless banished from the conscious knowledge of Hashem.
column15: And this is “a mighty hunter before the Lord”—akin to what the Sages stated (Chullin 7b) regarding sorcery: “that they diminish the heavenly entourage”; for in truth all their energy derives from holiness, but that force is bound under their grasp to act perversely, opposite to the true design of holiness. And Scripture elaborates (Genesis 10:10): “And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar” — meaning, because Nimrod observed the conclusion of the Flood taking place in Shinar, as stated in Zevachim (113b): Why was it called Shinar? Because all the corpses of the Flood were shaken out (nin'aru) there.

column11: I Samuel 14:6: ‘Jonathan said to the attendant who carried his arms, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of those uncircumcised fellows. Perhaps GOD will act in our behalf, for nothing prevents GOD from winning a victory by many or by few.”’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (I Samuel 14:6) to illuminate his exposition here (“Wherefore they are titled "uncircumcised" throughout Scripture: "let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised" [I Samuel 14:6], uttered by Jonathan who represents holy Yesod like Mashiach ben Yosef, coming...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And this laughter issues from the inner delight and joy within the soul, being a masculine rung (d'dechura), wherefore it possesses supreme potency; while the laughter over His creatures receives its stimulation from outside entities, being a feminine rung (d'nukva), wherefore it lacks intrinsic power; and therefore all songs uttered in this world over the downfall of the idolaters are formulated in the feminine gender (shirah), which indicates weakened vigor.

column15: “Count for yourself seven weeks, from the time the sickle is first put to the standing corn shall you begin to count seven weeks.” (Devarim, 16:9)“From the time the sickle is first put to the standing corn.” That is to say, at a time when man begins to march on towards victory he must possess a settled mind and make careful deliberations, for seven weeks represents great refinement.

column13: For Abraham sifted and purified all evil desires until he merited the Covenant in his flesh, which is the sign of that complete refinement, possessing no lust for evil, all desires being consecrated to Hashem. And this is woven into nature from birth and womb; thus by virtue of this covenantal sanctity he is not permitted to enter at all, merely standing at the portal without stumbling into the lust itself, for "your people are all righteous," and even uncircumcised Israelites are called circumcised.

column15: The Tabernacle and its vessels mirror the spiritual anatomy of Man and the order of Creation, as taught in Tikkunei Zohar (Introduction 13a): the Ark containing the Tablets corresponds to the innermost point of the heart and mind, the Menorah to enlightened intellect, and the Table to sanctified action—for when a person refines himself, he becomes a living Sanctuary.

column13: As it is written: "for all the firstborn are Mine; on the day that I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I hallowed unto Me all the firstborn in Israel" (Numbers 3:13). And it is stated: "All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up" (Psalms 75:11)—in the exact matter wherein the former is severed, the latter is exalted; and it is stated: "I shall be replenished, now that she is laid waste" (Ezekiel 26:2), which our Sages expounded (Megillah 6a): Caesarea and Jerusalem, if one is full the other is desolate, meaning that both occupy one identical level in the realm of sovereignty.

column15: “As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you, etc.” (Genesis 17:4). The concept is: Hashem told Avraham our Father, peace be upon him, that from His divine perspective he was born circumcised without unholy expansion, and from His side he had no inherent need for contraction; yet you on your part shall guard My covenant to contract yourself, and through this you will hold an active share in the bond you have with Hashem.

Rather, the community of Israel in that generation, before the miracle, cried out over this: “What has he done,” etc., on account of the root of “a time,” etc., “they have voided Your Torah,” which was established within him.

And at the death of Saul and Jonathan, who were the root of covenantal holiness in...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And this operates from the supernal Wisdom of King Solomon, peace be upon him, as I wrote elsewhere that David and Solomon correspond to Adam and Noah, being the Heart and the Brain [of bodily striving], Adam having sinned through a coveting heart, and Noah having sinned through intoxication which strips away Wisdom and "takes away the discernment of the elders"; and by virtue of his father's inheritance Solomon's nourishment was "grass" [and barley, and we already hinted on folio 39a in the mystery of the Omer offering that through barley unfolds the refinement of the physical body], whereas from his own dimension it was herds of cattle.
column15: Retaining only minimal vitality for the preservation of the species, to leave a surviving seed for the future. Wherefore all wild and domestic beasts dwelled together without harming one another, individual predatory drives being suspended. In the World to Come, however, when “the wolf also shall dwell with the lamb,” this harmony will not stem from weakness, but because Hashem will shine His great light, the earth filling with knowledge, revealing that all was given from One Shepherd, generating cosmic peace.

column11: II Samuel 1:20: ‘Tell it not in Gath,Do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon,Lest the daughters of the Philistine rejoice,Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (II Samuel 1:20) to illuminate his exposition here (“And at the death of Saul and Jonathan, who were the root of covenantal holiness in that generation, David mourned: "lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph" [II Samuel 1:20], regarding the Philistines who are...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And the Mekoshesh whose passion for Torah was so intense, yet whose halakhah was revealed only through his death, lacked personal fulfillment, retaining only the yearning; hence he had only daughters, and through them this passage was revealed, inheriting his spiritual power at his death when his desire reached fulfillment.
column15: For they were the third generation from Adam, the primordial light having been veiled step by step, making them feel severed from their Root, possessing free choice to do good or evil, the pristine certainty of Adam having vanished. Therefore they sought to invent an independent certainty on their own, yet directed it not toward divine service, but to serve their own selfish ends: namely, adopting a superficial subconscious awe so that they could indulge all bodily lusts at will—the fountainhead of all idolatry—.

column11: I Samuel 18:25: ‘And Saul said, “Say this to David: ‘The king desires no other bride-price than the foreskins of a hundred Philistines, as vengeance on the king’s enemies.’”—Saul intended to bring about David’s death at the hands of the Philistines.—’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (I Samuel 18:25) to illuminate his exposition here (“And this was why Saul demanded of David to marry his daughter with a hundred foreskins of the Philistines [I Samuel 18:25]; for David saying "I am a poor man and lightly esteemed" meant in spiritual stature, the...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And likewise vengeance is mentioned between two divine Names only when Heaven's Name surrounds him, bringing retribution on his foes; "And David was prudent in all his ways" (I Samuel 18:14) and prospered, "and Hashem was with him"—the Name of Heaven accompanying him wherever he turned, bringing success. This means that through action realized in reality, one receives reward in actuality—namely, the physical downfall of enemies, matching Keilim (29:9): "Action overrides action and thought, but thought cannot override action."
column15: As found with King David: only when told “the Lord tells you that He will make you a house,” did the thought arise in his heart to build a Temple for Hashem; and not as it appears to mortal sight, that the initiative begins with human choice for which Hashem rewards him later; for the reverse is true: human pursuit of God is merely the sign that Hashem chose him first, from which sprang his yearning.

column11: I Samuel 18:23: “And Saul’s servants spoke those words in the ears of David. And David said: ‘Seemeth it to you a light thing to be the king’s son-in-law, seeing that I am a poor man, and lightly esteemed?’” Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (I Samuel 18:23) to illuminate his exposition here (“for David saying "I am a poor man and lightly esteemed" meant in spiritual stature, the king's holiness being immense, demanding an equally holy son-in-law; and David humbled himself before all; wherefore Saul...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: But this confirms the very essence of my words: for the "Book of the Wicked" is the Book of divine Thought of the Blessed Name; wherein Israel arose in primordial Thought and were engraved there; and for Jewish sinners there remained no spiritual attachment except within this supreme book exalted above all, they being those who possess a portion in the World to Come; and the adversaries of David HaMelech, whom he had already severed through the Holy Spirit from the World to Come (like Doeg and Achitophel), he prayed that they be blotted out even from this book.
column15: And he strides with that vitality to serve Hashem and proclaim the Shema, an entire burnt-offering is truly forged from all those forces. Yet Adam HaRishon, seeing clearly that Hashem’s light radiated through all creations with immense clarity, considered this task of elevating creations back to Hashem superfluous, counting it a trivial matter; hence “for man there was not found a helper opposite him”—finding in creations no opposing resistance to holiness through which he could be aided in his labor of elevation.

column11: Bereshit Rabbah 70:11: ‘“He said to them: Is he well [hashalom lo]?” – is there peace [hashalom] between you and him? “They said: He is well,” – but if it is prattle that you seek: “Here is Rachel his daughter, coming with the sheep.” That is what is said: Speech is found among women. “He said: Behold, the day is still great, it is not time for the livestock to be gathered; give the sheep to drink, and go and herd” (Genesis 29:7). “He said: Behold, [the day] is still…” – he said to them: ‘If you are hired watchmen, “the day is still great.” If you are herding your own, “it is not time for the livestock to be gathered.”’ “He was still speaking with them, and Rachel came with her father’s flock; for she was a…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Bereshit Rabbah 70:11) to illuminate his exposition here (“And behold the Sages stated [Bereishit Rabbah 70:11]: there is no tribe lowlier than Dan, being among the feeble trailing behind whom the Cloud ejected, giving Amalek a hold to smite their hindmost, mocking: "Take...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: That rest and cessation should themselves constitute holy divine service, only through the love of Abraham. “Only this shall you take from my hand, for a witness that I have dug this well”, and from me emerged the true revelation of the service of Hashem, blessed be He. And King David, peace be upon him, is likewise the level of Shabbat as is known to initiates, and as noted that Judah is the polar opposite of Dan, and therefore represents the perfection of deeds.
column15: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.” This is what Scripture states (Psalms 92:1–2): “A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day: It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing praises to Your Name, Most High.” “Bereishit” (In the beginning) refers to the matter that the Blessed Name clarified and refined all the foundational elements, and this is encompassed within the word “Bereishit”; as we have seen that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, his entire holy labor was focused on the word “Bereishit,” refining and recombining the word “Bereishit” in seventy ways throughout the Holy Zohar and the Tikkunim.

column11: Deuteronomy 25:18: ‘how, undeterred by fear of God, he surprised you on the march, when you were famished and weary, and cut down all the stragglers in your rear.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Deuteronomy 25:18) to illuminate his exposition here (“being among the feeble trailing behind whom the Cloud ejected, giving Amalek a hold to smite their hindmost, mocking: "Take what You chose!"; harboring the dross of Micah's idol who rebelled against "I am Hashem,"...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And from this it is necessary for them to remove His providence from this world entirely — [holding] that perhaps someone [else brought it about], etc. — and of itself, since the essence of “coming-into-being is chance,” then all is “chance” — and this is the root and “the first of the nations” in the power of Amalek and Bilaam. you on the way [asher karcha ba-derech]” — the Sages read Amalek as the power of “chance” (mikreh / keri), cooling the recognition of providence; and Shemos 17:16, “Hashem has a war with Amalek from generation to generation” — Amalek being, as here, the root that would reduce all existence to happenstance.

column13: Section 14: Mordechai's Five Royal Garments Matching the Five Soul-Levels, Shatnez in the Girdle, and Transforming Evil on Purim The theme: The five royal garments of Mordechai corresponding to the five soul-dimensions (Naran-Chai), the linen and wool girdle reconciling the two inclinations, and Purim sweetening the bitter into "very good". Scripture enumerates five royal items for Mordechai: blue (techelet), white (chur), a crown of gold (ateret zahav), fine linen (butz), and purple wool (argaman) (Esther 8:15). These correspond to the five levels of the soul: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah.

column11: Megillah 14b: ‘Esther was also a prophetess, as it is written: “And it came to pass on the third day that Esther clothed herself in royalty” (Esther 5:1). column11: Bereshit Rabbah 3:4: ‘Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak asked Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman, saying to him: ‘Since I have about you that you are a master of aggada, [I ask you:] from what was the light created?’ He said to him: ‘It [the verse] teaches that the Holy One blessed be He wrapped himself in it like a garment, and the aura of its radiance shone from the end of the world to its end.’ He said it to him in a whisper. He said to him: ‘It is an explicit verse: “Wrapped in light as if with a garment” (Psalms 104:2), and you say it to me in a whisper? This is bewildering.’ He said to him: ‘Just as I heard it in a whisper, so I said it to you in a whisper.’ Rabbi Berekhya said: Had Rabbi Yitzḥak not expounded this in…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Bereshit Rabbah 3:4) to illuminate his exposition here (“And it is impossible to perceive His divine light hidden in the Torah and His Shechinah in the Holy of Holies, except for one whose bodily flesh is holy unto his God and all his passions directed toward Heaven, as...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Recounting how he personally witnessed with the Baal Shem Tov the manifestation of this hidden light, and that he also instructed him in this holy path how to attain this wondrous perception; see there his sweet holy words. And as is renowned throughout the entire world, our holy master HaKohen, the author, may his merit shield us, was the living treasury of the entire Oral Torah, and through the abundance of his sanctity, purity, piety, and asceticism, he merited to integrate all holy virtues.
column15: From this awakens in man the yearning for Hashem's light, stirring an intense cry in the human heart: “How and through what can I approach the light of Hashem, for He is awesome!” And this is why he stated that from there the light was created—meaning the sacred awe radiating from the site of the Temple. And according to the opinion that He cloaked Himself in a garment of pure light from which illumination emerged—the inner meaning is: that light reaches man when he roars within his heart: “Is it conceivable that I am severed, heaven forbid, from the Blessed Name who binds and unifies the entire cosmos unto Himself!”

column11: Berakhot 17a: ‘After his prayer, Rabbi Alexandri said the following: May it be Your will, Lord our God, that You station us in a lighted corner and not in a darkened corner, and do not let our hearts become faint nor our eyes dim. Some say that this was the prayer that Rav Hamnuna would recite, and that after Rabbi Alexandri prayed, he would say the following: Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to perform Your will, and what prevents us? On the one hand, the yeast in the dough, the evil inclination that is within every person; and the subjugation to the kingdoms on the other. May it be Your will that You will deliver us from their hands, of both the evil…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Berakhot 17a) to illuminate his exposition here (“and as the Sages prayed: "It is revealed that our will is to do Your will, only the yeast in the dough obstructs us" (Berakhot 17a), as Maimonides explained (Hilchot Geirushin 2:20) regarding coercing a man until he...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Not desiring to know good and evil, through which he could sink into false imagination. And the essential nature of Israel is so, as written in Berachos (17a): "It is revealed and known before You that our will is to perform Your will, and what prevents us? The yeast in the dough and the subjugation of the kingdoms, etc."; and both are one, for when the yetzer hara is eradicated from the world, the idolatrous nations will likewise be nullified and become proselytes drawn along (Avodah Zarah 3b).
column15: And concerning this it is said (Proverbs 10:9): “He that walks uprightly walks surely; but he that perverts his ways shall be known”: “He that walks uprightly”—this is one who stands in humility before Hashem, crowning Him over all, taking no pride in strength or wealth, as taught in Berakhot (40b): upon seeing bread he exclaims: “How beautiful is this bread, blessed is the Omnipresent who created it” — knowing he dwells in a world not his own, gazing toward the ultimate purpose; he possesses a shield on the day of Hashem's wrath.

column11: Mishneh Torah, Divorce 2:20: ‘When a man whom the law requires to be compelled to divorce his wife 14:8), a man who was married to a woman for ten years without her bearing a child (Hilchot Ishut 15:7), a man who becomes afflicted by [constant] bad breath or an odor from his nose, one who becomes a collector of dog feces, a miner of copper or a tanner or one who becomes a leper (Hilchot Ishut 25:11-12) or a priest who marries a divorcee (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 17:7). does not desire to divorce her, the court should have him beaten until he consents, at which time they should have a get written. The get is acceptable. This applies at all times and in all places. or to the era when the Sanhedrin (the High Court of Law)…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this commentary and philosophical-halakhic exposition (Mishneh Torah, Divorce 2:20) to illuminate his exposition here (“as Maimonides explained (Hilchot Geirushin 2:20) regarding coercing a man until he says "I am willing." Wherefore in Israel an evil thought is not combined with deed while a good thought is combined, while among the...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.

column13: As Maimonides wrote (Hilchot Geirushin 2:20) on coercing a man until he says "I am willing," for the essential soul never desires sin; see there. Sin being merely accidental, repentance is effective, an accidental circumstance being capable of eradication. Evil being only an accidental mate to sinners, wherefore a divine decree for evil can be rescinded, while a decree for good is never rescinded (Berakhot 7a).
column15: And that which he answered, “The woman whom You gave to be with me”—means that his defense was that he was compelled to eat; for how was it possible that she should eat while I refrain, leaving her permanently in deficiency with no one to redeem her alongside her lack? And how could he abandon one who had been unified as one essence with him, as taught by the Ari, of blessed memory (Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar Rosh Hashanah, ch. 3), that a single wall joined both of them without any dividing partition between them (see above, section 61).

column11: Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1: ‘If he finished the field for the poor. The reference is to Tosephta 1:5: “If he did not give from standing grain, he must give from sheaves. If he did not give from sheaves, he must give from stacks. If he did not give from stacks, he must give from the grain heap. If he did not give from the grain heap before it was smoothed, he must first give terumah and tithes and only then peah.” See also Mishnah 1:6, Halakha 7:2, 4:1; an extended version is in Babli Baba qama94a., you say that peah devolves on the sheaves. Would peah turn back to the first ear from its sheaf if the entire field was cut.? Rebbi Yose said, let us learn peah of sheaves from peah of standing grain. Since peah from…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1) to illuminate his exposition here (“while among the nations inversely (Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1; Tosafot Kiddushin 39b); for their root stems from Amalek, the alien god within the body, the evil inclination; whereas in Israel evil is merely external...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Who belonged neither to the nations nor to Israel, she was destined to give birth to a rebellious son (Sanhedrin 107a). And the commandment of honoring parents is a precept held with great zeal by the nations, as stated regarding Esau (Bereishis Rabbah 65:16); and in Kiddushin (31a) and Yerushalmi Peah (1:1): to learn the boundary of honoring parents from the gentile Dama ben Netinah; and there: "All the kings of the earth shall praise You, Hashem, when they hear the words of Your mouth" (Tehillim 138:4)—upon hearing "Honor your father and mother," the kings of the earth praised Him.
column15: The meaning is: concerning man it is written: “And man became a living soul,” translated “a speaking spirit” — meaning he possesses the power of speech, the essence of which is mutual connection among human beings. As taught in Midrash Rabbah (Toldot 65:21) and the Jerusalem Talmud (Berakhot 1:1): an angel has no flexible joints (kefitzin) while man possesses flexible joints; hinting that an angel cannot elevate above its fixed rung, whereas man can leap and unite with rungs far higher than himself.
